title: osf review run: lens-driven agent review
summary: Adds `osf review run`, a new subcommand that selects review lenses for a change, runs installed coding-agent harnesses headless over each lens, verifies every quoted finding against the files, reduces the answers to a per-lens and whole-review verdict, and journals each answer and the decision. It ships a 20-lens catalogue, a reviewer roster of eight harnesses, a JSON Schema for reviewer answers, a builder-family detector that leaves a change's own model family out of the roster, and a GitHub workflow that runs the review from the base branch with the pull request's tree mounted read-only. Alongside it, `osf scan` gains a `scan-secret` rule and suppression markers now work for scan findings, with `--no-suppress` for CI.

nodes.label: osf review run
nodes.subtitle: review_run_exit_code
nodes.summary: The new subcommand. Resolves the base, loads the roster and threshold, runs the review, writes SARIF, optionally posts to a pull request, and maps the verdict to an exit code (0 pass, 1 fail, 2 could-not-run). `--warn-only` forces 0.

nodes.label: osf scan
nodes.subtitle: scan_cmd
nodes.summary: Gains `--no-suppress`, which ignores every osf-disable marker so CI reports everything. Suppression markers now apply to scan findings, validated against every rule id in the tool.

nodes.label: osf check
nodes.subtitle: run_check
nodes.summary: `scan` and `scan-staged` now honour suppression markers unless `--gate` is set, matching how `lint-writing` already behaved.

nodes.label: review_run::run
nodes.subtitle: orchestrator
nodes.summary: Loads the catalogue, assesses risk, selects lenses, runs reviewers per lens, journals every attempt and the decision, and returns the verdict plus printable lines and kept findings.

nodes.label: Lens catalogue
nodes.subtitle: lenses::load / select
nodes.summary: Loads 20 shipped lenses, then an organisation folder, then the repository's `.osf/review-lenses/*.toml`, a later file replacing an earlier lens of the same name. Selects lenses by always/triggered/high-tier rules and by path globs or earned signals.

nodes.label: Context assembly
nodes.subtitle: review_context::build
nodes.summary: Builds the prompt's context: the diff widened by the tier's depth, plus declared inputs (work item, acceptance criteria, decision records, architecture docs, entry points). Redacts secrets through the scan rules and caps the result at 60 KB.

nodes.label: Reviewer runner
nodes.subtitle: reviewers::run_one
nodes.summary: Starts one harness with an allow-listed environment, writes the prompt to stdin, enforces a timeout with a tree kill, extracts the answer from an optional envelope pointer, and retries once on an invalid answer.

nodes.label: Answer validation
nodes.subtitle: answer::extract_and_validate
nodes.summary: Validates a harness's final message against the review-answer JSON Schema, then checks the answer names the right lens and scores every criterion. Falls back to fenced code blocks, last to first.

nodes.label: Quote verification
nodes.subtitle: quotes::check
nodes.summary: Checks each finding's quote against the file and line it names, with a two-line tolerance and shape rules for short quotes. Only a VerifiedAnswer can be scored, so no unverified finding reaches the reducer.

nodes.label: Verdict reducer
nodes.subtitle: reducer::decide_lens / decide
nodes.summary: Turns answers into a per-lens verdict (two-family quorum, blocker veto, mean of criterion scores) and a whole-review verdict (weighted mean against the threshold; any could-not-run lens makes the review could-not-run).

nodes.label: Builder-family detector
nodes.subtitle: builder::detect
nodes.summary: Reads each commit's `Code-Generator:` trailer in the reviewed range and maps the model name to a family, so reviewers from the family that built the change are left out of the roster for that run.

nodes.label: Risk assessment
nodes.subtitle: risk::assess
nodes.summary: Now also parses the diff content to earn review-lens trigger signals (public surface, concurrency, new-file, repeated-logic, high-traffic path) and reads `[review] hot_paths` from the trusted config root.

nodes.label: Journal
nodes.subtitle: journal::Payload
nodes.summary: Two new payload kinds, ReviewAnswer and ReviewDecision, both graded `reported`. The replay hash drops a review answer's transcript path so a rerun hashes the same.

nodes.label: process::kill_tree
nodes.subtitle: shared tree kill
nodes.summary: The tree-kill helper moved out of moon.rs so both the moon runner and the reviewer runner can kill a timed-out child and its descendants.

nodes.label: codex
nodes.subtitle: openai family
nodes.summary: Shipped roster entry, disabled by default. Runs `codex exec` with `--output-schema` pointing at a file; the whole stdout is the answer.

nodes.label: claude-code
nodes.subtitle: anthropic family
nodes.summary: Shipped roster entry, disabled by default. Runs `claude --print --output-format json` with an inline `--json-schema`; the answer is read from the envelope's `/structured_output`.

nodes.label: dsh
nodes.subtitle: deepseek family
nodes.summary: Shipped roster entry, disabled by default. Runs `dsh --profile headless`; no model flag, no schema flag.

nodes.label: opencode variants
nodes.subtitle: glm, kimi, qwen, mimo
nodes.summary: Four shipped roster entries reaching their model through OpenRouter, each pinned with `--model` in provider/model form. All disabled by default.

nodes.label: omp
nodes.subtitle: multi-family
nodes.summary: Shipped roster entry, disabled by default, with no credential variable named until a deployment fills one in.

nodes.label: [review] config
nodes.subtitle: config::review_config
nodes.summary: Reads the `[review]` table of osf.toml: roster overrides, threshold, timeout, cost ceiling, builder-family aliases and hot paths. Kept out of the layered Config so a fractional threshold does not break its Eq derive.

nodes.label: Shipped lenses
nodes.subtitle: defaults/review-lenses
nodes.summary: Twenty lens files compiled into the binary, six of which run on every change. Two more under `examples/` ship but are never loaded.

nodes.label: Shipped roster
nodes.subtitle: defaults/review-roster.toml
nodes.summary: Eight reviewer entries, one per harness installed in the development container, every one disabled until a repository turns it on.

nodes.label: Agent table
nodes.subtitle: agents::reviewer_harnesses
nodes.summary: Each supported agent now carries the harness name its roster entry uses, and a test fails when the roster's harness set drifts from this list.

nodes.label: review.yml
nodes.subtitle: pull_request_target
nodes.summary: Checks out the base branch as the only code it runs, checks out the pull request's head as data, builds osf from the base tree, and runs `osf review run` with the pull request's tree mounted read-only. Fork pull requests are gated behind an explicit variable and a protected environment.

nodes.label: ci.yml
nodes.subtitle: scan --no-suppress
nodes.summary: The scan step now passes `--no-suppress`, so a suppression marker added by a change cannot silence a finding in CI.

nodes.label: moon review task
nodes.subtitle: osf review run --if-enabled --warn-only
nodes.summary: A pre-push task that skips cleanly when no reviewer is enabled and never gates on its own exit code, since it runs in the builder's own workspace.

flows.title: One lens through the review pipeline
flows.summary: How a single selected lens turns into a verdict: context is built and redacted, each enabled reviewer's harness is started for its rounds, answers are validated and their quotes checked, and the reducer decides the lens.

messages.label: build(lens, depth, sources)
messages.note: The diff, widened by the tier's depth, plus any declared inputs. Secrets are redacted through the scan rules and the result is capped at 60 KB.

messages.label: redacted context
messages.note: A declared input that cannot be found makes the whole lens could-not-run, naming that input.

messages.label: run_one(reviewer, prompt, lens, timeout)
messages.note: Two rounds per family, until two non-builder families have answered.

messages.label: spawn with allow-listed env, prompt on stdin
messages.note: Only PATH/HOME/LANG and the reviewer's own credential variable reach the child; every other reviewer's key stays out.

messages.label: stdout
messages.note: A harness that exits non-zero, times out or cannot start counts as could-not-run for that lens.

messages.label: extract_and_validate(raw, lens)
messages.note: The answer is unwrapped from its envelope pointer, validated against the schema, and checked for the right lens and a score per criterion.

messages.label: Answer or reason
messages.note: An invalid answer is asked for once more with the reason appended; a second failure is reported invalid.

messages.label: check(root, answer)
messages.note: Each finding's quote is checked against the file and line it names, with a two-line tolerance.

messages.label: VerifiedAnswer + dropped
messages.note: Only a VerifiedAnswer can be scored, so an invented quote can never veto a lens.

messages.label: decide_lens(lens, answers, single_family_available)
messages.note: Two distinct families are required unless the roster only ever offered one; a blocker or must-fix finding vetoes the lens whatever its score.

messages.label: LensVerdict
messages.note: Pass with a score, Fail with a score and blocker count, or CouldNotRun with a reason.

steps.heading: Select the lenses
steps.body: Risk assessment sets the tier and the signals; the catalogue turns those into the lenses this change earns.

steps.heading: Build and redact the context
steps.body: The diff is widened by the tier's depth, declared inputs are added whole, and secrets are redacted before any reviewer sees it.

steps.heading: Run the harnesses
steps.body: Each enabled reviewer's harness is started for its rounds, with only its own credential in the environment.

steps.heading: Verify the quotes
steps.body: Every finding's quote is checked against the file and line it names; an invented quote is dropped before scoring.

steps.heading: Decide the verdict
steps.body: Two families must answer, a blocker vetoes the lens, and the weighted mean of lens scores is compared to the threshold.

steps.heading: Run it from the base branch
steps.body: The workflow builds osf from the base tree and mounts the pull request's tree read-only, so a change cannot weaken its own review.
